pages.text: "Found it! Crescent bread behind the shelf!" Coco reached a paw under the shelf. Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread, came in with a jingle of the doorbell. Coco's tummy rumbled. "This is my breakfast!"
The bread Coco pulled out had little blue spots. "Pretty spots. Is it sprinkled with candy?" Without checking, Coco brought it to their mouth. Even though it smelled sour, Coco opened wide.
Grandpa hurried over and caught Coco's paw. "No, Coco! That bread has spots!" Startled, Coco closed their mouth. "Oh? It isn't candy?"
Coco set the bread on the kitchen dough table. "Mom, can I eat this?" Mom shook her head. "That's mold. It can give you a tummy ache. Good job asking." Coco drew their paw back.

Mom put fresh crescent bread beside the spotted bread. One had blue spots and a sour smell; the other was golden and smelled delicious. "Your mouth is a precious door," she said. "A door for delicious bread."
Mom taught three promises. "One, spotted bread? Don't eat it! Two, sour smell? Don't eat it! Three, not sure? Ask Mom!" Coco nodded three times. "I can keep those promises!"

A little later, Coco saw another spotted loaf under a shop basket. This time was different! Coco tucked their paws behind their back. "Spotted bread? Don't eat it!" Coco called, "Mom, another one here!"
Mom looked and smiled wide. "Well done! You called instead of eating it!" Coco straightened proudly and tightened the scarf knot with both paws. Grandpa clapped. "Ho ho! Coco knows it all!"
Before picking up bread, Coco always sniffed. "One, spotted bread? Don't eat it! Two, sour smell? Don't eat it! Three, not sure? Ask Mom!" Mom dropped the spotted bread into the bin.

Mom lifted Coco and pressed their cheeks together. Grandpa smiled, holding delicious bread. "Even if you want it, don't put anything strange in your mouth." Coco nuzzled Mom's cheek. "Spotted bread? Don't eat it!"
